title: Credo Brands Marketing Ltd - 544058 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Mufti (Credo Brands) is a store-count-flat, throughput-led year: FY27 guided to ~20 openings and ~20 closures, mid-single-digit same-store growth at best, and EBITDA margin seen at 23–24% on higher ad spend.

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 6% YoY to INR162 crore with EBITDA flat at INR42 crore; management guides FY27 to flat store count and mid-single-digit same-store growth at best.
summary.overview: Credo Brands (Mufti) reported Q4 FY26 revenue up 6% YoY to INR162 crore, with gross margin of 58.8% and EBITDA flat at INR42 crore (25.6% margin) as advertising was stepped up to about 8% of revenue. FY26 revenue was flat at INR592 crore, with EBITDA of INR154 crore (26% margin). The company closed 24 stores and opened 7 in the quarter, reducing the network by 17. Management said FY27 is a consolidation year with roughly 20 openings and 20 closures, with ad spend rising to 8-10% of revenue and margins likely lower.

segments.name: Retail (EBO stores)
segments.commentary: Store count fell by 17 QoQ: 7 opened and 24 closed in Q4. Same-store sales were flattish for the quarter, though lower for the full year; revenue per sq ft about INR11,700 (as cited by an analyst, stable).

segments.name: Online / omnichannel
segments.commentary: Online channel is about 9% of revenue, of which the company's own platform is about 5%. Website business grew about 75% YoY in FY26; online EBITDA margin is lower because it is still discount-driven.

guidance_outlook: FY27: store count broadly flat, with about 20 closures and about 20 openings; throughput per store is the focus.
FY27 growth: management would be happy with mid-single-digit same-store growth; FY27 described as a consolidation year, with visibility limited by West Asia conflict and inflation.
Advertising and branding spend to rise to about 8-10% of revenue; Raman KV's 9-10% framing was confirmed as the broad direction, but not fixed.
FY27 EBITDA margin may be about 23-24%, lower than FY26's 26%, because of higher marketing spend.
Gross margin expected in a 56-58% range, though management said it could fall to 55%.
Capex of about INR40-45 lakh per new store, depending on high street or mall location.
capex_capacity: Q4 FY26 net store count reduced by 17: 7 opened, 24 closed.
FY27 plan: about 20 new stores and about 20 closures, so the count stays roughly flat.
As of the call date there were 31 stores in the new Mufti 2.0 identity: 14 renovated, 16 new and 1 relocated.
Capex per new store is INR40-45 lakh, varying by location (high street vs mall).
Store transition to the new identity to be gradual over 2-3 years, timed to lease expiries and renewals.
Tier 3 expansion will be cautious and limited to strong locations.
demand_pricing: Consumer sentiment was cautious through FY26, with uneven discretionary spend and weak footfall; management said near-term demand visibility is poor.
Loyalty programme Muftisphere has 2.5 million members; 35-40% of members are active, with an average ticket size of about INR5,200.
Pricing: management said Mufti has not raised prices, only premiumised brand perception. Gross margin is protected by passing on cost rises and favourable terms with vendors.

Input costs are very high: suppliers are quoting at astronomical levels, and cotton (candy) has risen to about INR62,000 per candy. No forward contracts are used; seasonal contracts are business commitments.
Online AOV is below store AOV; new stores have not yet stabilised after 6-7 months of operation.
Receivable days are about 140-146 under the risk-absorption model. Management says receivables are not overdue, and there have been no material bad-debt or inventory write-offs historically.

qa_highlights.question: How many stores were opened and closed in Q4, and what are the same-store sales and premium-store productivity trends?
qa_highlights.answer: 7 opened and 24 closed in Q4. Same-store sales were flattish in the quarter, lower for the full year. Early indicators for new premium stores are encouraging but too early to quantify.

qa_highlights.question: What is the store growth and revenue outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About 20 openings and 20 closures, so the store count stays flat. Management would be happy with mid-single-digit same-store growth, but visibility is poor.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 margins hold at 26%?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The CFO said FY27 EBITDA margin may be about 23-24% because marketing spend is rising. Gross margin is expected in the 56-58% range.

qa_highlights.question: How has the debtor-days position changed and is it overdue?
qa_highlights.answer: Debtor days are in line with the business model and may move 5-10%. Receivables are not overdue, and the company expects to stay structurally above some peers.

qa_highlights.question: Will ad spend fall to 4-5% in FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not say. Ad spend should pay back more before it is escalated further, and it will respond to market conditions.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the gross margin expansion, and how is raw material inflation being handled?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said FY26 gross margin expansion was mainly product mix. Management said it will pass costs through, with no forward hedging, and sees the 56-58% range holding.

risks_watch: Same-store sales are flat in Q4 and FY26 declined. FY27 SSSG target is only mid-single-digit, with no guarantee.
Input cost inflation (cotton, fabric) and the West Asia conflict could push gross margin toward 55% and weigh on demand.
Ad spend rising to 8-10% of revenue may compress EBITDA margin to about 23-24% in FY27.
Receivable and inventory days are structurally high (about 140-146 debtor days); watch for any change in overdue receivables.
Tier 3 rollout is slower and more cautious after post-COVID consumer behaviour changed.
Dividend: management said INR2 per share was announced, which an analyst had questioned.
summary.management_tone: Cautious and measured on near-term demand, citing geopolitical risk and inflation, with FY27 called a consolidation and transition year. Confident on long-term brand and premiumisation strategy, but specific FY27 numbers were given with qualifiers such as "calls we take on our feet". Management was evasive on FY28-29 targets and on cost outlook.
key_quotes: So, this is not the correct year to be looking at growth perspective.
We are not trying to build the fastest-growing brand for 1 or 2 years.
We have not premiumized our prices, so to say, or gone higher in terms of our prices.
our margins should be looked at annually because that is more rational way to look at our margins.

adds.what: ~20 new EBO stores planned in FY27 (store count held roughly flat with ~20 closures)

growth.why: FY27 is guided as a consolidation year with flat store count (~20 openings, ~20 closures), mid-single-digit same-store growth only as a hope, and EBITDA margin falling to 23-24% from 26% on higher ad spend; demand visibility is poor, so growth backing is vague.
